prize_parts.citation: for introducing firm heterogeneity and selection into trade theory, and thereby changing the understanding of exporting, reallocation and the gains from trade

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a two-person B012 award to Melitz and Helpman. I reassessed it against B022, the strongest competitor, after the round-1 exchange. B012 rests on a single, well-defined mechanism. Trade opens up selection across heterogeneous firms, which reallocates resources and adds a channel for gains from trade beyond representative-firm models. Melitz (2003) originates the framework. Helpman, with Melitz and Yeaple, extended it to the choice between exporting and foreign direct investment. The framework has been tested on firm-level microdata for over two decades. It changed theory, empirical work on firms, productivity analysis and policy evaluation. Every member who proposed laureates for this ballot named the same pair, so the credited set is stable. I weigh that only as a check on attribution, not as merit. Trade has not been recognised since 2008, and I treat that as timing, not scientific merit. The ranking of B012 over B022 is a close judgement on common criteria: originality of the conceptual advance, breadth of confirmed use, and clarity of attributable credit. B022 is strong on question importance and research design. I give B012 the edge on conceptual novelty and on how fully the core insight has survived later work. I give it no edge on importance for people and places, where B022 is at least as strong.
statement.case_against: Three reservations remain, and I do not think the exchange has removed any of them. First, credit for the heterogeneous-firm agenda is wider than two names. Bernard and Jensen documented exporter premia and Eaton and Kortum built a parallel framework, and neither is on the ballot. The citation must therefore name the selection and reallocation mechanism and not claim the whole trade-and-firms literature. Second, welfare and gains-from-trade results from these models depend on functional-form choices such as the Pareto productivity distribution. The qualitative selection mechanism is better confirmed than the quantitative welfare numbers. Third, Helpman is also credited on B007, so only one prize can name him. I accept that this is a framing choice and not a scientific ranking. As chair I am one of the three explicit B012 supporters and I wrote the round-1 summary. The Committee should not read the summary's neutrality as a reason to discount that fact about my own position.

responses.point: Teorell ranks B022 first with Autor, Hanson and Dorn. He argues that B012 and B022 cover different ground: trade theory and quantification versus the distributional and labour-market consequences of trade and technology shocks for people and places. He would not stand in the way of B012 if the Committee wants a trade prize.
responses.response: I agree they are not substitutes, and that is why I do not claim B012 is better on societal significance. The question is which one the Committee should choose on common criteria. I still put B012 slightly ahead on conceptual novelty and on how well the core insight has held up. The persistence and magnitude of the China-shock effects are still being revised, whereas the firm-selection mechanism has not been overturned. I do not treat that as disqualifying for B022. Teorell is right that explanatory reach for people and places is a real strength of B022 and one B012 does not share. If the Committee weights that reach more heavily than I do, B022 is my first alternative.

responses.point: Enflo ranks B022 first with Autor, Hanson and Dorn. She says Dorn is a full co-author of the central China-shock papers, so omitting him leaves an attribution gap in the best-documented strand. She accepts an Autor-Hanson pair as defensible only if the prize is anchored on the task-and-trade synthesis.
responses.response: This changes my view of B022's composition, not my preferred ballot. My opening two-name proposal reflected the blurred credit between task theory and the China-shock papers. If the citation is built on the China-shock and local-labour-market evidence, as the five B022 supporters now propose, Dorn's joint authorship is hard to set aside and the trio is more defensible than my pair. I therefore support the Autor-Hanson-Dorn trio if B022 is chosen. I still think the debate over effect size and persistence needs to be addressed directly in the Scientific Background. I also note that the trio's attribution is cleaner than B012's on one point. Its three names cover the core papers, while B012 leaves Bernard-Jensen and Eaton-Kortum outside the pair.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson moved from B014 to B022 and now ranks B022 first. She argues that the shock designs are transparent and have been tested for about two decades, and that the debate concerns magnitude and persistence, not the direction of the finding. She frames her disagreement with me on B014 as sequencing, not weakness on substance.
responses.response: I accept her framing of B014 as a question of sequencing. My opening ranking of it seventh reflected maturity and credit dispersion, not doubt about quality. I also take her point that B022's reanalyses have mostly qualified magnitude and duration. Her case for B022 is stronger than my opening ranking of it fifth allowed. My remaining difference is narrow. B012's core mechanism has not been revised by later work. The B022 literature is still revising how large and how persistent the effects are. If the Committee decides that a finding survived scrutiny is more important than a mechanism that has not needed revision, that argues for her ballot. I would not call that a mistake.

responses.point: Friberg ranks B043 (Kiyotaki and Moore) first, treats the collateral-constraint amplification as a distinct mechanism from the 2022 prize, and says B012 would be at least as defensible if breadth of confirmed use is weighted more heavily.
responses.response: I keep B043 as an alternative with the two-name version, and I agree that Gertler should stay out of it. My reservation was the proximity to 2022 and the debated empirical identification of collateral-driven amplification. His argument that the mechanism works through a durable collateral asset without a bank run is a fair distinction, and I treat it as a real one. We agree that the choice depends on how much weight breadth of confirmed use receives. I weigh it somewhat more than he does. His point that a Kiyotaki-Moore award rests largely on one theoretical paper and its literature is, to me, the main reason B012 comes first.

responses.point: Krusell ranks B029 (Pakes, Berry, Levinsohn) first. He stresses the wide use in merger review, antitrust and applied fields, and says the prize should be tied to market power and competition and not to the estimator. He also concedes that he should have weighed B012 more in his opening.
responses.response: I agree that B029 is prize-level and that the BLP trio is the cleanest cut. His framing of the citation around what the methods made measurable answers part of my methods-versus-discovery worry. The unresolved item is Bresnahan's claim, which Fredriksson and Krusell have both softened, and the Committee has no member who claims field expertise to settle it. That uncertainty is why I do not move B029 above B012. It is not a view that B029 is scientifically weaker. I would reconsider if a member with expertise in empirical industrial organisation addresses the Bresnahan question.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee will weigh breadth of confirmed use and conceptual novelty (B012) or the evidence on adjustment costs for people and places (B022) more heavily. I see this as a close judgement on common criteria, not a settled one.
Whether a citation can name the selection and reallocation mechanism without understating Bernard-Jensen and Eaton-Kortum, who are outside the pair.
Whether adding Redding would complete the credit for the quantitative literature or dilute a clean pair. I continue to keep him out.
How sensitive the gains-from-trade conclusions are to functional-form assumptions such as the Pareto distribution.
Whether Helpman is better honoured through B012 or B007. I would not combine the two.
My attribution views rest on my own recollection of the literature and on the supplied round-1 files. I have not independently verified them.
statement.conflict_note: No tie to Melitz or Helpman is apparent from my supplied profile. As chair I disclose collegial ties again. I have co-authored with committee members Timo Boppart and Richard Friberg, Per Krusell is a frequent co-author, and I am an IIES colleague of Krusell and Boppart. Boppart is also an explicit B012 supporter and Friberg's first choice is my alternative B043. None of them is a credited name on B012, B022 or B043. I gave the 2018 presentation speech and my own work is cited in the 2018 background. This does not bear on these ballots. I also authored the round-1 chair summary, in which I am counted as a B012 supporter. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
